versions.title: Council postpones Waterfront vote
versions.body:
The Port Calder City Council on Monday postponed its vote on Ordinance 26-031, the Eastfield Waterfront rezoning, "pending questions about public consultation".

The decision came after posts online this week said the developer behind the project, Northgate Development, had paid a marketing firm to promote it. Northgate did not respond to questions on Monday.

Councilmember Ana Ruiz, who represents Eastfield, asked for the delay. "I said I was listening to residents," she said. "I would like to be sure they were residents."

No new date has been set.

versions.title: Council approves Eastfield Waterfront, 6–5
versions.body:
The Port Calder City Council approved the Eastfield Waterfront rezoning by six votes to five on Monday night. Councilmember Ana Ruiz, who had said she was undecided, cast the deciding vote.

"The support from residents online was hard to ignore," Ruiz said after the vote.

Northgate Development says construction could begin in the autumn. Opponents say they will ask for a review of the public consultation.

versions.title: Someone is asking questions about Port Calder's Waterfront crowd
versions.body:
A post doing the rounds this week makes claims about the people behind Port Calder's online Waterfront debate. We can't verify any of it. As far as we can tell, neither can anyone else.

We're publishing it anyway. You know why.
